name: Apache Spark
summary: A distributed dataflow engine that builds lazy transformations over partitioned datasets, schedules jobs as dependent stages and tasks, and runs each application through an isolated driver and executor set.

features.name: Driver and executor application boundary
features.description: A Spark application has a driver program that creates SparkContext and coordinates work, plus an independent set of executor processes that run tasks and store application data. Cluster managers allocate those executors and Spark ships application code to them.
benefits: Isolates applications from one another at executor and scheduling boundaries
Allows Spark to use standalone, YARN, or Kubernetes resource managers
Makes application coordination and worker execution explicit
costs: The driver must remain network-addressable to executors
Data is not shared between Spark applications without external storage
Driver failure and executor lifecycle affect distributed job progress

features.name: Lazy partitioned RDD lineage
features.description: An RDD is a partitioned distributed dataset that supports transformations and actions. Transformations are lazy and record how to derive a dataset; an action materializes the required computation, and lost partitions can be recomputed from lineage.
benefits: Enables optimization before computation is materialized
Provides parallel work units through partitions
Allows recovery by recomputing lost derived partitions
costs: Repeated actions can recompute uncached lineage
Partitioning and shuffle choices control data movement
Lineage recovery trades storage overhead for recomputation time

features.name: DAG, stage, and task scheduling
features.description: Spark turns an action's dependency graph into jobs, stages, and tasks. A stage groups work across partitions around shuffle boundaries, and tasks are sent to executors; scheduling can also coordinate multiple jobs within one SparkContext.
benefits: Exposes parallel task scheduling while retaining dependency structure
Uses shuffle boundaries to separate stages with different data dependencies
Supports FIFO or fair scheduling for concurrent jobs
costs: Shuffle introduces network, disk, and serialization cost
Long-running stages can delay later jobs under FIFO scheduling
Task locality and stragglers influence end-to-end latency

features.name: Application-scoped persistence and shared variables
features.description: Spark can persist RDD partitions in memory, on disk, or with replication for reuse within an application. Broadcast variables distribute read-only values to workers, while accumulators support aggregated updates from tasks.
benefits: Avoids repeated recomputation for reused datasets
Provides explicit mechanisms for read-only distribution and aggregation
Keeps cached data scoped to the application's executor set
costs: Cached data competes for executor memory and storage
Persistence policies affect recomputation and eviction behavior
Shared-variable semantics differ from ordinary driver-side mutation

mathematical_views.question: How does a lazy dataset transformation graph determine the partition computations needed for an action?
assumptions: RDDs are vertices with partition sets and dependency edges
Transformations are evaluated only when an action requests results
The view abstracts optimizer and scheduler implementation details

mathematical_views.question: Which distributed task execution traces implement a job's dependency graph across shuffle boundaries?
assumptions: Stages are formed from dependency and shuffle boundaries
Each task processes one or more input partitions on an executor
The model treats scheduling policy and failures as explicit transition parameters

benefits: Application isolation with interchangeable cluster managers
costs: Driver reachability and executor lifecycle become correctness concerns

benefits: Parallel lazy computation and lineage-based recovery
costs: Recomputation and shuffle costs depend on graph shape
Shuffle and scheduling policy add latency and operational tuning

benefits: Efficient reuse and explicit distributed shared-value mechanisms
costs: Executor memory, storage, and eviction become application constraints
